co_wigwam_creek_lost_creek_wilderness.blurb: A wilderness of more than 100 square miles in Colorado's South Platte country, south of Highway 285 and west of Highway 126 near Deckers. The rock is Pike's Peak granite, formed into big domes and buttresses with a few towers. Climbing is mostly multi-pitch trad on cracks and friction, with a separate set of boulder problems alongside. Roped routes cluster between 5.9 and 5.12, and the boulder problems run from V1 to V9. Approaches are often several miles on trails. Cro Magnon holds the most climbs, followed by McCurdy Park Tower and Wigwam Dome. Wigwam Dome faces south, takes a lot of sun, and has routes of up to seven pitches.

ct_god_s_country.blurb: A bouldering area in West Rock State Park, with problems scattered along the foot of West Rock's west-facing cliffs. It sits high on the hillside with no roads in view, so it feels secluded, and the walls catch afternoon sun. Nearly everything is bouldering, with only a few trad lines. Grades lean easy to moderate, with most problems between V0 and V3 and a tail of harder ones up to V8. At A Midsummer Nightsession, boulders sit beside trad lines on a cliffline above the main cluster. Divine Manifestations holds the most climbs, followed by Tibbs Area, A Midsummer Nightsession and Kyle's Slabs.

id_lost_river_range.blurb: Idaho's tallest range, running north to south in the central part of the state with Highway 93 along its west side between Arco and Challis. It holds seven of the state's nine 12,000-foot peaks, including Mount Borah. The range is known for loose, chossy rock, with exceptions. The climbing is varied: sport and trad on the walls, alpine routes on the big peaks, and ice that forms each year. Rock routes mostly run 5.10 to 5.12. Ramshorn Canyon is the main sport venue, with limestone, mostly bolted lines and some four- to six-pitch routes, and Cedar Creek has more sport climbing. Bear Creek Wall holds the most climbs.

il_pere_marquette_state_park.blurb: Limestone bluffs overlooking the Mississippi River near Grafton, about an hour from St. Louis. The rock is featured limestone, giving short vertical lines, spread over named walls. Sport routes and boulders are close to equal in number, with a smaller group of trad lines. Sport grades run from about 5.6 to 5.12, clustering around 5.7 and 5.10, while the boulders mostly fall between V0 and V3. It suits beginner and intermediate climbers well. Jungle Book holds the most climbs, followed by Lily Wall, Lily Boulders and Eagle Wall.

me_mdi_bouldering.blurb: Boulders scattered across Mount Desert Island in Acadia National Park, mostly along the coast between Otter Cliffs and Sand Beach. Almost all of it is bouldering, with problems from V0 to V5 making up the bulk and a handful of much harder ones. Beech Cliff holds the most climbs: a large boulder field on Beech Mountain near Somesville with easy and moderate problems alongside harder ones. Great Head Proper centres on a sea cave that faces the ocean, and is a cave-bouldering area. School House and Monument Cove are among the other bigger sub-areas.

mn_little_foxx_canyon.blurb: A bouldering-focused canyon area in the Duluth area, split into four sub-areas: North Little Foxx, South Little Foxx, Foxx Rocks and Little Foxx. Bouldering dominates, with a handful of roped climbs, up to 50 feet at Little Foxx and 40 feet at Foxx Rocks. Boulder grades range from V0 and below up to about V6, with most between V0 and V5. South Little Foxx is exclusively bouldering, mostly high problems that finish on slopey or slabby tops. North Little Foxx holds the most climbs, followed by South Little Foxx and Foxx Rocks.
